items.title: 'Lifeline' or 'catastrophe'? Community divided over proposed data centre
items.description: To its supporters, this proposed data centre will provide much-needed regional jobs, but in the nation's driest state, critics say the draw on river water to cool the machines could be too great.

items.title: Zelenskyy warns 'Moscow will burn' as Russian capital comes under attack
items.description: Scores of drones targeted Moscow overnight in what was Ukraine's largest attack on the Russian capital.

items.title: Global telco escapes penalty for bank scam texts despite customers losing millions
items.description: A global telco that failed to stop more than 1,000 scam text messages from reaching Australians has faced no consequences, the ABC can reveal.

items.title: Hanson's 'scary' parental leave views outdated, advocates say
items.description: Pauline Hanson's openness to discuss a winding back of paid parental leave is concerning and harks back to an Australia that no longer exists, advocates say.

items.title: Man arrested after boy critically injured in crocodile enclosure at UK zoo
items.description: British police say they have arrested a man on suspicion of attempted murder after being called to a popular zoo north of London.

items.title: Migration dips as Coalition accuses government of failing to meet targets
items.description: Net overseas migration remained above 300,000 last year, fuelling opposition claims Labor has locked in an unsustainable new normal despite the number of arrivals continuing to fall.

items.title: Live: South Africa snatch late draw, US star in serious doubt for Socceroos clash
items.description: South Africa leave it late to snatch a 1-1 draw with Czechia, as Group A is blown wide open in Atlanta. Meanwhile, US talisman Christian Pulisic doesn't train ahead of his side's clash with the Socceroos. Follow live.

items.title: Hegseth blasts NATO members, announces review of US forces in Europe
items.description: He said that too many NATO allies failed to support the US on Iran in what he called a "shameful" denial of access, basing and overflight.

items.title: Gina Rinehart says Qld should give some of its islands to Elon Musk
items.description: The mining magnate, speaking at the National Bush Summit, also talked about how she believed Townsville could become a base for the Israeli military.

items.title: Crows legend Tony Modra seriously injured in crash
items.description: Crows legend Tony Modra has been seriously injured in a truck crash.

items.title: The curious case of Dan Sullivan vs Dan Sullivan at the US primaries
items.description: A Democrat is accused of being a Republican in disguise; a Republican is accused of being a Democrat plant. It's primaries season in the US, and suspicions of dirty pool are rife.

items.title: Ancient oak tree linked to the legend of Robin Hood is dead
items.description: The tree is said to have sheltered Robin Hood, the legendary 13th-century bandit who stole from the rich and gave to the poor and took refuge in the Nottingham forest.

items.title: Bruce Lehrmann makes legal bid for Brittany Higgins documentary footage
items.description: Former Liberal staffer Bruce Lehrmann has asked a court to order the company behind a film involving Brittany Higgins to hand over raw footage.

items.title: Dockers beat Cats for 13th straight win, as Bolton takes incredible mark
items.description: Fremantle comes from behind to beat Geelong for a 13th straight game, as Shai Bolton hits the heights at Perth Stadium with a Mark of the Year contender.

items.title: Are old buildings the solution to new homes?
items.description: From former post offices to pumping stations, there are buildings with commercial histories all around Australia. Could repurposing them into homes help with the housing supply?

items.title: Friday news quiz: Soccer celebrations, bin battles, phone fails and weather watching
items.description: Today's news quiz is heating up like El Niño. Will you strut like an internet-famous duck or get schooled like Prince George?

items.title: No princesses, no musical numbers: How Toy Story changed children's cinema
items.description: The multi-billion-dollar franchise has overcome rewrites, accidental deletions and generations of changing tastes to bring Toy Story 5 to cinemas in 2026.

items.title: Government buys back $430m worth of water for Murray-Darling Basin
items.description: A $430 million Murray-Darling Basin water buyback sparks a fresh political fight over the balance between food production and environmental recovery.

items.title: Auditors unsure when Snowy 2.0 will be finished
items.description: An audit into the mega hydro-electric project in the NSW Snowy Mountains has outlined five recommendations.

items.title: Fans push back against Trump administration's anime posts
items.description: Both fans and the Japanese government push back after a series of Trump administration posts using images from popular anime and manga.

items.title: Eviction notice for elderly Melbourne renter ruled invalid
items.description: HousingFirst has lost its bid to repossess the inner-east Melbourne property of an elderly tenant who disputed the validity of a rental increase.

items.title: Mental health concerns raised weeks before Aubrey Donahue's death, inquest hears
items.description: The inquest heard Mr Donahue's mother had shared concerns about his mental health in the weeks leading up to his death.

items.title: How Max Plath became Queensland's newest Origin cult hero
items.description: The players who fill the spaces in between the stars are the secret to Queensland's Origin dominance and in Max Plath the Maroons have found yet another player who knows just how to do it.

items.title: Fashion boss was 'scary and violent' in alleged rape, trial hears
items.description: A woman says she was scared to leave the Byron Bay holiday home of a Melbourne man, who she alleges forced her to engage in 11 non-consensual sex acts over a four hour-period.

items.title: Coroner suggests racism marred investigation of Indigenous teen's death
items.description: The mysterious death of Mark Haines, whose body was discovered on railway tracks in northern NSW in 1988, would have been treated differently "if it was a white boy", according to the coroner.
